defense_analyst.prose: Carolina's pass rush is volume-based: the Panthers sack on 4.4% of dropbacks [dc1] over 388 dropbacks [dc2] and post a pressure proxy of 11.6% [dc3]. Tampa Bay has allowed a pressure proxy of 15.2% [dc4], so TB's protection is the weaker link, and the staff should expect Carolina to bring extra rushers. CAR sends 5+ rushers on 30.9% of dropbacks [dc5], averaging 4.3 rushers [dc6], which ranks 15th in blitz rate [dc17]. Our split of blitz rate by down is not broken out here, so prepare for pressure on every down rather than only third down. Against the run, CAR averages 6.4 defenders in the box [dc7] over 250 run plays [dc8], a moderate count that leaves room for TB's perimeter runs if the protection holds. In the passing game, Carolina allows explosive plays on 5.7% of pass plays [dc9], so big-play upside exists but is not outsized. Red zone is the sharper signal: opponents score touchdowns on 75.9% of red-zone drives [dc10], though that rests on only 29 drives [dc11]. Third down is the clearest opening, with opponents converting 46.2% [dc12], ranked 28th of 32 [dc13]. On offense, TB has been sacked on 9.3% of dropbacks [dc14] and ranks 22nd in average depth of target [dc15], so the attack leans short-to-intermediate and must win third down against a defense that gives up conversions.
